report:
### Conclusion
**Supported.** Medical evidence from clinical trials and meta-analyses demonstrates that preoperative skin preparation with chlorhexidine-alcohol reduces the risk of surgical-site infections (SSIs) following cesarean delivery compared to iodine-alcohol or povidone-iodine formulations.

### Key Evidence
* **Randomized Controlled Trials:** A pragmatic randomized trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* concluded that preoperative skin antisepsis with chlorhexidine–alcohol resulted in a significantly lower risk of SSI after cesarean delivery than iodine–alcohol. Similarly, a clinical trial comparing chlorhexidine-alcohol to povidone-iodine-alcohol found a significantly lower rate of SSIs in the chlorhexidine group (6.95% vs. 14.28%).
* **Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses:** A systematic review evaluating preoperative antiseptics specifically for cesarean delivery confirmed that skin cleansing with chlorhexidine-alcohol reduces SSIs compared with povidone-iodine solutions. Furthermore, a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials reported that alcohol-based 2% chlorhexidine possessed the highest probability of effectively preventing SSIs, outperforming alcohol-based povidone–iodine.

### Sources
1. New England Journal of Medicine: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048
2. International Journal of Reproduction, Contraception, Obstetrics and Gynecology: https://www.ijrcog.org/index.php/ijrcog/article/view/6461
3. PubMed Meta-Analysis: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/
4. ScienceDirect: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282
